summary: Sporadic 5xx spike from HTTP/2 stream prioritization + GPU init thundering causing runtime exits
description:
Issue summary:
During an afternoon tenant burst we observed a sharp, short-lived elevation in 5xx responses from the API gateway for a single dedicated customer (NovaReply). Errors aligned with a rapid ramp of many concurrent HTTP/2 streams that used the high-priority class. Upstream runtimes began exiting with process-level errors during repeated GPU initialization attempts, producing a cascade of 502/503 responses from the gateway.

Impact:
- NovaReply reported ~30% of requests failing with 5xx for ~8 minutes starting 2026-03-13T15:12 UTC.
- Customer traffic volume: sustained tens of qps spiking to hundreds of concurrent streams.
- Customer's critical routes (chat generation + embeddings) affected; saw user-facing timeouts and rapid retries.

Environment:
- prod - us-east (dedicated pool for NovaReply)
- API Gateway (HTTP/2) -> ingress proxy -> runtime pool (dedicated GPU nodes)
- Affected models: redwood-curie-v1 (chat), redwood-embed-1 (embedding uploads)

Observed symptoms / logs:
- APIGW: many 502/503 entries with upstream reset and "upstream: connection reset by peer"
- Proxy logs: large number of HTTP/2 PRIORITY frames and many half-closed stream traces
- Runtime logs (sample): "gpu_init: retry 3/5 - NVML_ERROR_TIMEOUT", followed by "process exited with signal SIGABRT" and "watchdog: restart requested"
- Kernel and driver: short bursts of nvml timeouts and driver -> process-level reclaims reported at 2026-03-13T15:13:05Z
- Scheduler: a rapid burst of pod/ephemeral worker starts concurrently during tenant warmup

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Simulate many concurrent short-lived HTTP/2 streams using high-priority class to the same dedicated tenant route.
2) Trigger embedding + chat mixed workload with small payloads and frequent reconnects.
3) Observe short window of GPU init concurrency on a fraction of runtime nodes and subsequent process exits.

Initial hypothesis:
- Prioritization + HTTP/2 stream scheduling caused an ingress fan-in pattern that concentrated init work on a small set of runtime nodes (asymmetric load).
- The asymmetric fan-in coincided with autoscaler/backfill behavior causing simultaneous cold starts; multiple processes attempted NVML initialization in parallel, triggering driver timeouts and process exits (thundering init).
- Gateway retries/hedged retries amplified the traffic into the same high-priority slot, worsening contention.

Mitigation applied (2026-03-13):
- Support applied a temporary priority-shed rule at APIGW to demote newly created streams from high-priority to normal for NovaReply for 15 minutes (reduced immediate 5xx).
- SRE added a conservative ramp-up flag on the autoscaler to stagger ephemeral worker starts for the dedicated pool (hotfix rollout in progress).
- Customer advised to spread embed + chat requests and avoid simultaneous reconnect storms while we stabilize.

Next steps / remediation plan:
- Short-term (in progress): keep priority-shed rule for 6 hours and monitor 5xx rate and runtime restarts. Roll out autoscaler stagger fix to the rest of the dedicated pool if stable.
- Mid-term: implement ingress-side rate limiter for high-priority class per-tenant to prevent asymmetric concentration, add guard in serving-runtime to serialize NVML init when contention detected.
- Long-term: add heuristic to scheduler to spread cold starts across more nodes and add a NVML init backoff across processes on the same host.

Customer communication plan:
- Notified NovaReply CS contact at 2026-03-13T15:25 UTC with status and workaround.
- Planned update EOD 2026-03-13 and a follow-up once staggered autoscaler rollout completes.
investigation_notes:
Timeline summary:
- 15:12 UTC: NovaReply reports elevated 5xx.
- 15:13 UTC: initial SRE alert: runtime pod restarts in dedicated pool.
- 15:15 UTC: traced to NVML timeouts and SIGABRT in runtime processes.
- 15:20 UTC: applied APIGW priority demotion; 5xx rate dropped by ~70% within 2 minutes.
Findings:
- Pattern differs from prior general OOMs: here GPU driver reported timeouts during init, not persistent OOM.
- Heap / CPU usage on nodes remained normal; driver telemetry shows spikes in NVML init latency.
- Autoscaler attempted to create ephemeral workers aggressively to satisfy backlog; no explicit quota exceeded but cold start concurrency high.
Open questions:
- Why did init attempts concentrate on a subset of nodes? (scheduler affinity / recent patch?)
- Do specific model variants trigger slower NVML init under particular library paths?
resolution_notes: Partial remediation: APIGW priority demotion + staged autoscaler ramp reduced 5xx to baseline within 10 minutes. SRE will monitor for 24 hours. Permanent fixes scheduled: ingress per-tenant priority rate limiter (next week) and NVML-init serialization (sprint 2). No rolling rollback required. Customer to be offered an incident postmortem and recommended traffic-shaping guidance.
